comment: Which upstream handler services which chrome.send message on
astro://management, and which of those messages the Astro page sends.
The management page adopts ONE upstream handler wholesale, the same move
the settings page makes with fifteen. This file is what
tools/tests/lib/scan-adopted-handlers.py joins the page's sends against:
a message the page sends that no installed handler registers is not an
error anyone sees -- WebUIImpl::ProcessWebUIMessage reaches
DUMP_WILL_BE_NOTREACHED, fatal in a DCHECK build and a SILENT NO-OP in the
release build users get.
THE THREE MESSAGES THAT ARE DECLARED AND DELIBERATELY NOT SENT are the
promotion banner's: shouldShowPromotion, setBannerDismissed and
recordBannerRedirected. The banner opened Google's admin console with a
campaign parameter and reported the click; Astro does not draw it. They
stay declared because the handler is upstream's and adopted UNMODIFIED, so
it still registers them -- the honest statement is that nothing sends
them, not that nothing could. The scanner's unsent-message direction is
what keeps that a recorded decision rather than drift.
Message list transcribed from RegisterMessages() in
chrome/browser/ui/webui/management/management_ui_handler.cc at the locked
revision, non-ChromeOS branch: the four ChromeOS-only messages
(getLocalTrustRootsInfo, getFilesUploadToCloudInfo, getDeviceReportingInfo,
getPluginVmDataCollectionStatus) are not registered on Linux and are not
listed.

ManagementUIHandler.note: Enterprise policy state: whether the browser is managed, what it reports, and which extensions, applications and websites the administrator configured. Adopted wholesale and unmodified.
